## Analysis

**Comparability:** Both periods come from the same source (the FY2024 10-K consolidated statements of operations), are presented on the same accounting basis, and Amazon's fiscal year ends December 31 with no 53rd-week or segment-redefinition mismatch between them [DOC: amzn_growth.txt — Amazon.com, Inc. Form 10-K FY2024, accession 0001018724-25-000004]. So FY2023 and FY2024 growth rates are directly comparable. (Caveat: the excerpt provides only reported, as-stated net sales — no FX-neutral/constant-currency breakout is available, so the comparison is on a reported basis.)

**Net sales** [DOC: amzn_growth.txt — FY2022 $513,983M; FY2023 $574,785M; FY2024 $637,959M]:

| Period | Net sales | YoY growth | Absolute increase |
|---|---|---|---|
| FY2022 | $513,983M | — | — |
| FY2023 | $574,785M | **+11.83%** | +$60,802M |
| FY2024 | $637,959M | **+10.99%** | +$63,174M |

**Interpretation:** The growth rate decelerated slightly, by roughly 84 basis points (11.8% → 11.0%). Notably, this is a *rate* deceleration driven by the larger revenue base — the absolute dollar increase actually grew, from $60.8B in FY2023 to $63.2B in FY2024. Given the magnitude (<1 percentage point), this is best characterized as a marginal deceleration / essentially stable low-double-digit growth rather than a meaningful slowdown.

ANSWER: Decelerated slightly — growth slowed from ~11.8% in FY2023 to ~11.0% in FY2024 (a ~0.8 pt decline), essentially flat low-double-digit growth, with absolute dollar sales gains still rising ($60.8B to $63.2B).
